category_overview: All six tools are Microsoft products that share one identity, permission and compliance plane (Entra ID, Microsoft Graph, Purview), but they sit on two different licensing stacks. Microsoft 365 Copilot (now marketed as "Microsoft Copilot") is a per-user add-on, and Copilot in Word, Excel and Teams are not separate products but surfaces of that single licence; the free Copilot Chat tier gives enterprise-data-protected chat without the in-app features. Power BI Copilot and Power Automate belong to the Fabric/Power Platform stack, which is priced by capacity (Fabric CU) or by maker/bot licence plus consumption-based Copilot Credits, so the "Copilot" label hides very different cost models. Overlap is real: Teams recap competes with Teams Premium, Excel Copilot and Power BI Copilot both answer data questions, and Power Automate cloud flows compete with Copilot Studio agent flows. Enterprises already on Microsoft 365 E3/E5 usually standardise on the Copilot add-on (or the new E7 bundle) for knowledge workers, Power BI on Fabric capacity for analytics, and Power Automate Premium plus a governed Centre of Excellence for automation, while using Purview and DLP as the common control layer.

tools.name: Microsoft 365 Copilot
tools.vendor: Microsoft (Microsoft Copilot family; product renamed from "Microsoft 365 Copilot" to "Microsoft Copilot" in August 2026, licences may still carry the old name)
tools.what_it_is: An AI assistant embedded in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, Teams, Loop and OneNote, plus the standalone Microsoft Copilot app (copilot.cloud.microsoft) with Chat, Search, Notebooks, Pages and agents. It grounds large language models in the user's Microsoft Graph content (mail, files, chats, meetings) while honouring existing permissions.
key_capabilities: Graph-grounded chat with optional web grounding and citations
Researcher and Analyst reasoning agents producing reports, decks and data analyses
Copilot Notebooks and Pages for persistent, shareable working context
Edit with Copilot (Agent Mode) that makes multi-step changes inside Word, Excel and PowerPoint
Copilot Cowork task delegation and federated Copilot connectors over MCP (GA Sept 2026)
Agent Builder and declarative agents governed from the Microsoft 365 admin center
tools.enterprise_data_handling: Paid licence and no-cost Copilot Chat (Enterprise Data Protection): prompts, responses and Graph data are not used to train foundation models; data is encrypted, tenant-isolated and covered by the DPA. Copilot surfaces only content the user can already view and honours Purview sensitivity labels; admins get retention policies, audit and eDiscovery over Copilot interactions. EU traffic stays in the EU Data Boundary, but Anthropic-provided models and Bing web queries are excluded from it; data-residency commitments (ADR/Multi-Geo) apply since 1 March 2024. Stated compliance: GDPR, ISO 27001, ISO 27018, ISO 42001, HIPAA (not web queries); Microsoft Copilot is listed in-scope for Office 365 GCC/GCC High/DoD FedRAMP, and Office 365 SOC 2 Type 2. Admins choose whether OpenAI or Anthropic subprocessor models are used.
tools.licensing_pricing: Add-on priced at USD 30 per user per month on annual commitment (USD 360/year) per independent 2026 guides; Microsoft's own pricing page could not be retrieved. Included in Microsoft 365 E7 (USD 99 per user per month, GA 1 May 2026, bundling E5, Copilot, Agent 365 and Entra Suite). Copilot Business for tenants up to 300 users (independent source: USD 21). Prerequisite plans include M365 E3/E5/F1/F3, Business Basic/Standard/Premium, Office 365 E1/E3/E5 and others; GCC, GCC High and DoD add-ons exist. Copilot Chat is no-cost with eligible M365 subscriptions; some newer models and features bill via Copilot Credits.
tools.integrations: Microsoft Graph (Exchange, SharePoint, OneDrive, Teams), Copilot connectors including MCP-based federated connectors, Power Platform connectors (separately licensed), Dataverse/Dynamics search, Purview, Planner agent, Copilot Analytics in Viva Insights.
tools.recent_developments: Aug 2026: app renamed Microsoft Copilot with new URL (MC1454108); Learn docs now state "Microsoft 365 Copilot is now named Microsoft Copilot". 1 May 2026: Microsoft 365 E7 launched with Copilot included. 22 Apr 2026: Agent Mode GA in Word/Excel/PowerPoint. Sept-Oct 2026: Copilot Cowork, Vision, federated connectors GA, GPT-6.1 Sol and Claude Sonnet 5.5 under usage-based billing, Pages moving to OneDrive storage.
tools.best_fit_departments: Strong for Office of the CEO, Board Secretariat, HR Business Partnering, PMO, Sales, Legal drafting, Learning & Development and any role living in Outlook/Teams/Word. Weak fit where the listed task is structured-data or system-specific: Accounts Payable invoice extraction (Power Automate/AI Builder), Supply Chain demand insights and Enterprise Applications & ERP (Power BI/ERP tools), and specialist Regulatory Compliance control evidence.
tools.training_notes: Learners must master grounding prompts with files and people, verifying citations, sensitivity labels and oversharing hygiene, when to use Researcher/Analyst versus chat, reviewing Agent Mode edits, and Notebooks. Core 6-10 hours for general users; Advanced 12-20 hours for agents, Notebooks and Analyst; Specialist 20-40 hours for Agent Builder, connectors and governance.
tools.caveats: Outputs are not guaranteed factual and must be reviewed. Permission hygiene is a prerequisite because Copilot exposes anything a user can already open. Government clouds lack several features (Edit with Copilot, Word/Excel/PowerPoint agents, scheduled prompts; web grounding off by default; Teams Copilot not in GCC High). EU Data Boundary excludes Anthropic models and web queries. Annual commitment plus emerging usage-based billing complicates budgeting, and the 2026 rename causes documentation confusion.

tools.name: Power BI Copilot
tools.vendor: Microsoft (Copilot in Power BI, part of Copilot in Microsoft Fabric)
tools.what_it_is: Generative AI built into Power BI Desktop, the Power BI service, Power BI apps and mobile. Business users chat with reports and semantic models in a report pane or a full-screen standalone Copilot; authors use it to create report pages, narrative visuals and DAX queries. It runs on Fabric capacity rather than a per-user licence.
key_capabilities: Summarise an open report or answer data questions in the report Copilot pane (GA)
Standalone cross-item Copilot that finds and queries any report or model the user can access (preview)
App-scoped Copilot with author-verified answers (preview)
Generate report pages, narrative visuals and summaries in email subscriptions
Write and explain DAX queries; create measure descriptions; Copilot in web modeling
Power BI data answers surfaced inside Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat (GA Sept 2026, separate licence)
tools.enterprise_data_handling: All tiers: processed by Azure OpenAI Service hosted by Microsoft (admin may opt in to OpenAI as subprocessor); data is not used to train models and is not available to other customers; prompts are not stored after the session and there is no abuse-monitoring retention. Copilot only reads data the user can access, with RLS/OLS enforced. Data stays in the capacity's region unless the tenant admin enables the cross-geo processing setting, which is required (and off by default) outside the US and EU. Tenant admins can disable Copilot; sovereign clouds are unsupported. Fabric provides encryption at rest and in transit, customer-managed keys, Private Link, multi-geo residency and Purview labels/DLP. Power BI cloud service is listed in scope for SOC 2 Type 2, ISO 27001 and FedRAMP.
tools.licensing_pricing: No per-user Copilot SKU: requires paid Fabric capacity F2 or higher or Power BI Premium P1+; trial, Pro or PPU alone are insufficient. Usage is metered in capacity units: 100 CU-seconds per 1,000 input tokens (10 cached), 400 per 1,000 output tokens. Power BI Pro USD 14 and Premium Per User USD 24 per user per month (annual); Pro is included in Microsoft 365 E5 and Office 365 E5. Independent pricing (Oct 2026): F2 about USD 262.80/month PAYG, F64 about USD 8,409.60 PAYG; Azure's pricing page did not render figures. A Fabric Copilot capacity can centralise Copilot billing for Pro/PPU workspaces and Desktop.
tools.integrations: Microsoft Fabric (OneLake, Data Factory, data agents), Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat, Excel export, Teams, Purview, Dynamics/Dataverse and SQL sources via Power BI connectors; relevant to FP&A, People Analytics, RevOps, PMO and Supply Chain reporting.
tools.recent_developments: Apr 2025: Copilot opened to all paid SKUs from F2. Standalone Copilot turned on by default Sept 2025; prompt limit raised to 10,000 characters. Aug 2026: Copilot summaries read visuals hidden behind bookmarks. Sept 2026: agentic report authoring GA, Power BI answers in M365 Copilot Chat GA, model-level Copilot restrictions GA, Microsoft 365 Copilot in Power BI preview. Q&A visual retiring Feb 2027. Fabric Copilot capacity documentation refreshed Oct 2026.
tools.best_fit_departments: Best for Business Intelligence & Analytics, FP&A, People Analytics, Sales/Revenue Operations, Supply Chain, Service Delivery, PMO and executive consumers. Weaker for Market Research & Competitive Intelligence (external data rarely modelled), Corporate Strategy scenario analysis (not a what-if engine), Internal Audit control testing, and Compensation/DEI where sensitive data demands strict RLS before enabling.
tools.training_notes: Model owners must prepare data for AI and mark models approved; authors need DAX review skills and prompt specificity using real field names; consumers need to read warnings and verify numbers; admins must monitor CU consumption and regional settings. Core 6-10 hours for consumers; Advanced 12-20 hours for report authors; Specialist 20-40 hours for model owners and capacity admins.
tools.caveats: Capacity cost and throttling are the main risk: an F2 can be exhausted by light use, and consumption rates can change. Standalone Copilot is preview and missing in several regions; English works best; sovereign clouds unsupported. Identical prompts are cached for 24 hours. Outputs can be inaccurate without curated models. Some third-party guides still state an F64 minimum, which is outdated.

tools.name: Excel Copilot
tools.vendor: Microsoft (Copilot in Excel, a surface of the Microsoft Copilot / Microsoft 365 Copilot licence)
tools.what_it_is: The Copilot pane and "Edit with Copilot" mode inside Excel on Windows, Mac, web and mobile. It analyses workbook data, writes and explains formulas, builds PivotTables and charts, applies formatting and, in editing mode, changes the workbook directly, including running Python. A separate Excel Agent in Copilot Chat creates new workbooks from a description.
key_capabilities: Generate, apply and explain formulas across multiple sheets
Surface insights as charts, PivotTables, trends and outliers
Edit with Copilot (Agent Mode): add or rename sheets, modify ranges, build tables and visuals in place
Plan mode that outlines steps before changing anything, plus a Show changes pane
Python in Edit with Copilot for statistics, simulations and transformations (Aug 2026)
Web grounding with citations and pulling data from other OneDrive/SharePoint workbooks
tools.enterprise_data_handling: Inherits Microsoft Copilot enterprise data protection: prompts, responses and workbook content are not used to train foundation models, are encrypted and tenant-isolated, and respect Purview sensitivity labels and usage rights. Interactions are retained and governable via Purview retention, audit and eDiscovery. If the organisation disables "connected experiences that analyze your content", Copilot in Excel is unavailable. Government clouds: Edit with Copilot is not yet available in GCC, GCC High or DoD, which limits structured-data analysis there. The Excel Agent in Copilot Chat is Frontier-stage and English-only.
tools.licensing_pricing: No standalone SKU. Requires the Microsoft Copilot add-on (independent 2026 guides: USD 30 per user per month, annual commitment) on an eligible Microsoft 365 plan, or Microsoft 365 E7 which includes Copilot. Consumer Microsoft 365 Personal/Family/Premium plans get Copilot in Excel with AI-credit limits. Copilot Business covers tenants up to 300 users.
tools.integrations: OneDrive/SharePoint (files should be cloud-saved with AutoSave for editing), Python in Excel, Power BI export, Copilot Chat Excel Agent, Word and PowerPoint for downstream reporting, Purview labels.
tools.recent_developments: 22 Apr 2026: Agent Mode became GA and the default experience, now surfaced as "Allow editing"/Edit with Copilot. 25 Aug 2026: Python support in Edit with Copilot (Windows, Mac, web). 14 Sept 2026: the preview =COPILOT() function was retired before GA; cached values remain but recalculation returns #NAME?. Excel Agent available in Copilot Chat for creating workbooks from prompts.
tools.best_fit_departments: FP&A (variance narratives, quick scenario tables), Accounting & Financial Reporting (reconciliation support, explaining inherited formulas) and Treasury (cash-flow scenario drafts) fit well as drafting and exploration aids. Taxation is a weaker fit: document extraction and tax research are better served by specialist tools, and Microsoft's own guidance warns against relying on Copilot for finance or legal decisions.
tools.training_notes: Learners must format data as tables with clear headers, keep files in OneDrive/SharePoint, understand Chat-only versus Allow-editing and Plan mode, verify every formula and Python output, use Show changes and version history, and know the retired COPILOT() function. Advanced 12-20 hours for finance teams; Core 6-10 hours for occasional users.
tools.caveats: Outputs are non-deterministic; an independent Oct 2026 test found inconsistent depreciation and WACC calculations. Not intended for decisions in finance, legal or medical domains without expert review. Workbooks that used =COPILOT() now break. Editing features depend on cloud-saved files and are missing in government clouds. Large or messy ranges reduce reliability.

tools.name: Microsoft Word Copilot
tools.vendor: Microsoft (Copilot in Word, a surface of the Microsoft Copilot / Microsoft 365 Copilot licence)
tools.what_it_is: The Copilot pane inside Word for Windows, Mac, web, iPad and mobile. It drafts documents from prompts and referenced files, rewrites and reformats selected text, summarises and answers questions about a document, and in Edit with Copilot (formerly Agent Mode) restructures whole documents in place. A Word Agent in Copilot Chat creates documents from a conversation.
key_capabilities: Draft from a prompt, outline, notes or referenced files (type / to pick sources) while reusing existing structure
Rewrite selected text for tone or concision; convert text to tables or images; add citations
Summarise long documents and chat about their content in Chat-only mode
Edit with Copilot: multi-step drafting, restructuring and formatting with reviewable changes
Model choice (Auto, Claude Sonnet or Claude Opus) depending on subscription and availability
Word Agent in Copilot Chat generating documents from web and tenant content
tools.enterprise_data_handling: Inherits Microsoft Copilot enterprise data protection: prompts, responses and referenced content are not used to train foundation models; access follows the user's permissions and Purview sensitivity labels; interactions can be retained, audited and discovered through Purview. Note that Anthropic (Claude) models selectable in Word are excluded from the EU Data Boundary and in-country processing commitments. Edit with Copilot and the Word Agent are not yet available in GCC, GCC High or DoD. Users remain responsible for verifying facts, citations and policy statements.
tools.licensing_pricing: No standalone SKU. Requires an eligible Microsoft 365 subscription plus the Microsoft Copilot licence (independent 2026 guides: USD 30 per user per month, annual commitment), or Microsoft 365 E7 which bundles Copilot. Copilot Business serves tenants up to 300 users; consumer Microsoft 365 Premium includes Copilot in Word with credit limits.
tools.integrations: OneDrive/SharePoint files, Outlook email and Teams content as references through Microsoft Graph, Copilot Notebooks, Copilot Chat Word Agent, Purview sensitivity labels and IRM; for Legal, pairs with contract repositories in SharePoint.
tools.recent_developments: 22 Apr 2026: Agent Mode GA and default in Word, since relabelled "Allow editing"/Edit with Copilot. Mid-2026: Claude Sonnet and Claude Opus selectable as models in Word. July 2026: improved source citations and section navigation in summaries. Sept-Oct 2026: Agent Mode rolled to Word for Android (MC1488843). Aug 2026 rename of the parent product to Microsoft Copilot.
tools.best_fit_departments: Legal Affairs (the only listed department) is a reasonable fit for first-draft clauses, summarising long agreements, tone rewrites and consistency checks. It is not a legal research or redline-comparison tool, and Microsoft states Copilot is not intended for conclusions in legal domains, so it should complement specialist tools such as CoCounsel rather than replace them.
tools.training_notes: Learners must master referencing source files, structuring briefs, Chat-only versus editing modes, reviewing Copilot edits as tracked changes, verifying every citation and defined term, applying sensitivity labels, and understanding model choice implications. Within Legal's Specialist track, allocate 12-20 hours to Word Copilot itself, with 6-10 hours for general staff.
tools.caveats: Fluent output can cite the wrong section; formatting drifts on documents beyond roughly 15-20 pages; privileged material must be label-protected before use. Choosing Claude models moves processing outside the EU Data Boundary. Editing features are unavailable in government clouds. Branding changes (Agent Mode, Allow editing, Edit with Copilot) confuse documentation.

tools.name: Microsoft Teams Copilot
tools.vendor: Microsoft (Microsoft Copilot in Microsoft Teams, with the Facilitator agent and intelligent recap)
tools.what_it_is: Copilot inside Teams meetings and events (up to 1,000 attendees), chats, channels and calls on Windows, Mac, web, iOS and Android. During a meeting it answers private questions about the discussion; afterwards it powers the recap with AI notes and tasks. The Facilitator agent joins meetings to take live Loop notes, track agendas and create tasks.
key_capabilities: Real-time meeting Q&A: who said what, where people agree or disagree, suggested follow-ups
Intelligent recap: AI notes, recommended tasks, chapters, speaker and personal timeline markers, audio and video recap
Copilot without saved transcript ("Only during the meeting") using temporary speech-to-text
Chat and channel catch-up: summaries, decisions, action items and shared links (30-day default window)
Facilitator agent: live Loop notes, agenda timers, Planner tasks (preview), Word document drafting
Summaries of Word files shared in chats
tools.enterprise_data_handling: Inherits Microsoft Copilot enterprise data protection (no training on tenant data, encryption, permissions). Prompts and responses are stored and can be retained via Purview, even in "only during meeting" mode in the Commercial cloud (not GCC/DoD). Post-meeting use requires a transcript, which becomes discoverable content; Facilitator notes are saved as .loop files in the initiator's OneDrive and treated as transcript data. Not available in end-to-end-encrypted meetings, in meetings hosted by other organisations, or in GCC High. Admins control behaviour through the meeting policy -Copilot setting (default: enabled with saved transcript required). Teams is in scope for Office 365 FedRAMP (GCC/GCC High/DoD), SOC 2 Type 2 and ISO 27001.
tools.licensing_pricing: Each participant needs a Microsoft Copilot licence (independent 2026 guides: USD 30 per user per month annual; included in Microsoft 365 E7) on top of a Teams licence. Intelligent recap alone is also available with Teams Premium (independent source: USD 10 per user per month, annual), but Copilot in meetings, audio and video recap, Facilitator and Interpreter require the Copilot licence. From 1 April 2026 some former Teams Premium features moved into Teams Enterprise.
tools.integrations: Teams meetings and Outlook calendar, Loop, Planner, OneDrive/SharePoint recordings and transcripts, Teams Rooms, Purview retention and eDiscovery, Viva Insights; for Board Secretariat, feeds minutes and action registers.
tools.recent_developments: Facilitator core features and Word document creation reached GA with Planner task tracking in preview (mid-2026). Audio recap, video recap and multilingual recap are in public preview (Learn, May 2026). 1 April 2026 Teams Premium/Enterprise licensing change. Aug 2026 rename to Microsoft Copilot. Events scaled to 1,000 attendees with organiser/presenter-only Copilot in large-audience events.
tools.best_fit_departments: Board Secretariat & Corporate Governance (the only listed department) fits for internal committee meetings: draft minutes, decisions and action registers. The fit weakens for formal board meetings with external directors (Copilot is unavailable in externally hosted meetings and E2EE meetings), and board confidentiality requires deliberate transcript, retention and label settings before use.
tools.training_notes: Learners must master meeting options (During and after, Only during, Off), transcription consent and notification, prompting during meetings, reconciling AI notes against the transcript before publishing minutes, Facilitator setup, and retention/eDiscovery implications. Core 6-10 hours, with an extra governance module for secretariat staff.
tools.caveats: After-meeting recap needs a saved transcript; AI notes and audio recaps can be inaccurate and audio recaps expire after 60 days. Facilitator works only in scheduled meetings, one language per meeting, and cannot be customised. Licensing between Teams Premium and Copilot is easily confused. GCC High lacks Teams Copilot.

tools.name: Power Automate
tools.what_it_is: A low-code automation service combining cloud flows (API and connector-based), desktop flows (robotic process automation), process and task mining, AI Builder document processing and a Copilot that builds flows from natural language. It lives in the Power Automate web portal and Teams app, the Power Automate for desktop application, and increasingly as agent flows inside Copilot Studio.
key_capabilities: Cloud flows over more than 1,400 connectors (SharePoint, Outlook, Teams, Dataverse, SAP, Salesforce, ServiceNow) with approvals and business process flows
Attended, unattended and Microsoft-hosted RPA for legacy systems
Process and task mining, including object-centric process mining (GA June 2026)
AI Builder document and invoice processing, prompts and classification, now consuming Copilot Credits
Copilot in the cloud-flow designer: create, edit, describe and explain flows in natural language
Governance via Managed Environments, DLP policies, advanced connector policies and audit logs
tools.enterprise_data_handling: All tiers: Copilot runs on Azure OpenAI within Azure; prompts and outputs are not used to train Microsoft or third-party models unless the tenant admin opts in; no eyes-on abuse review. Cross-region processing is admin-controlled (US and GCC in-region, EU inside the EU Data Boundary, other geos may route to the US). Dataverse uses TDE encryption with optional customer-managed keys; TLS 1.2+ in transit; Purview audit retains Power Automate events 90 days; DLP and environment rules govern connectors. Compliance: Power Automate is in scope for SOC 2 Type 2 and ISO 27001; Power Platform US Government supports FedRAMP High and DISA IL2/IL4/IL5. Copilot in cloud flows is available in GCC; disabling it requires a Microsoft support request.
tools.licensing_pricing: Premium USD 15 per user per month (annual): unlimited flows within 40k actions/day, premium connectors, one attended bot, process mining. Process USD 150 per bot per month and Hosted Process USD 215 per bot per month (250k actions/day, unattended bot). Process Mining add-on USD 5,000 per tenant per month. Pay-as-you-go via Azure (independent source: USD 0.60 per premium flow run). Microsoft 365 seats include only standard connectors at 6k actions/day with no RPA. Agent flows bill 13 Copilot Credits per 100 actions (free when an agent calls the flow for Microsoft 365 Copilot-licensed users). Seeded 5,000 AI Builder credits end 1 November 2026, replaced by Copilot Credits.
tools.integrations: SharePoint, Outlook, Teams, Forms, Dataverse, Dynamics 365, SAP and Salesforce connectors; AI Builder for AP invoice extraction; Approvals for facilities and vendor requests; Copilot Studio agents calling flows; Fabric export of process-mining models.
tools.recent_developments: AI Builder credits end-of-life 1 Nov 2026 (announced Oct 2025). Agent flows in Copilot Studio with one-way conversion of cloud flows. Advanced connector policies GA (June 2026). Desktop flow version control and version compare GA 13 May 2026; self-healing UI automation agent preview 31 Mar 2026; object-centric process mining GA 5 Jun 2026; shared Process capacity across flow groups GA 30 Jul 2026. Release plans archived Oct 2026 in favour of the AI at Work roadmap.
tools.best_fit_departments: Business Operations & Process Excellence is the strongest fit (process mining plus automation). Accounts Payable & Receivable fits for invoice extraction and exception routing but now carries Copilot Credit costs. Workplace Administration & Facilities fits for request routing and notifications, though organisations with ServiceNow may route tickets there instead.
tools.training_notes: Learners must master triggers, actions and connectors, error handling and retries, solution-aware flows, environment and DLP strategy, licensing and request limits, RPA basics, AI Builder credit consumption, and reviewing Copilot-generated flows before saving. Core 6-10 hours for approvers and consumers; Advanced 12-20 hours for makers; Specialist 20-40 hours for RPA, process mining and Centre of Excellence roles.
tools.caveats: Licensing is complex: premium connectors, request limits, flow ownership and the AI Builder-to-Copilot-Credits shift can raise costs 2-4x over list price. Copilot in the designer supports a subset of connectors and cannot fix flow errors. Third-party connectors move data outside Microsoft's compliance boundary. Agent flows stop when Copilot Credit capacity is exhausted. Trials are unavailable in government clouds.
